decision: Not adopted: a row saying that Claude Code's grep shell function skips gitignored files, so a recursive grep can print nothing and exit 1 while a match exists.
reopen_if: The grep-ignored-empty-nudge hook is removed or stops firing on an empty recursive grep, or a real session misses a match the hook did not flag.
why: The plugin's grep-ignored-empty-nudge hook already fires at the moment it matters: when a call running a recursive grep prints nothing, it tells the agent to re-run it through bash -c or command grep. The report also came from a scripted probe session, not from a real miss.

decision: Not adopted: a row saying BSD grep (FreeBSD, pfSense, macOS) has no GNU backslash escapes.
reopen_if: compuse-ssh drops that paragraph, or the trap shows up in local shell work with no ssh involved.
why: compuse-ssh already covers it in more detail: grep and sed, the trailing-backslash abort, the quoting layers between the local shell and the remote sh, POSIX classes, and copying the file back to parse it in Python. A remote host is also where the trap bites, so one copy there is enough.

decision: Not adopted: a row warning that awk's END block fires once after every file of a multi-file glob, so a per-file test written in END only sees the last file.
reopen_if: A baseline run without the skill gets awk END over several files wrong.
why: No gap: a clean-room baseline run without the skill, on a neutral task, already explained END, FILENAME, NR versus FNR, and gave both a per-file fix and a gawk ENDFILE form. The row would teach nothing the model does not already do.
